text:
In this Flutter monorepo (glasses_app at apps/glasses_app), I need to find the best place to add a one-time, fire-and-forget audio pre-warm task that runs as early as possible during app startup (independent of BLE connection state), to work around a known iOS cold-start audio engine warm-up cost.

Please investigate and report back:
1. Where is `main.dart` located for `apps/glasses_app`, and what does its startup sequence look like (roughly, up to and including `runApp`)? Is there an existing place where "app-level one-time startup tasks" are run (e.g. a bootstrap/init service, a Riverpod provider that's read once at startup, an `initState` in a root widget)?
2. Is there an existing Riverpod provider or service in `packages/core/core_audio` for constructing/obtaining the audio engine (e.g. `interpretationAudioEngineFactoryProvider` or similar) that already wires up `DefaultInterpretationAudioEngine`, `FlutterSoundTtsOutput`, etc.? Show me its exact location and definition.
3. Is there any existing "warm-up" or "prewarm" naming/pattern anywhere in the codebase (core_audio, feature_app_llm, or apps/glasses_app) — even a removed/deprecated one — that I should be aware of or could follow the pattern of? (Note: an iOS-specific TTS engine warm-up hack was tried before and removed as ineffective — I want to know exactly where that used to live and why it was removed, referencing harness/pitfalls.md if it explains it.)
4. Does the app already have a notion of "platform is iOS" checks (e.g. `defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.ios`) used elsewhere in core_audio, to see the established idiom for gating iOS-only behavior?
5. Report the exact file path and relevant code snippets (with line numbers) for all of the above so I can make an informed, minimal edit.

Do not make any code changes — this is a pure investigation/report task.
